items.quote: You have two ways to authenticate your MCP client: **OAuth** (recommended) or **API Key**.
items.why: Names OAuth and API key only. No bearer_token or PKCE detail.

items.quote: Clients are registered dynamically via RFC 7591 — no manual setup in a dashboard.
items.why: States dynamic RFC 7591 registration with no dashboard setup. Key part matches.

items.quote: Create an API key in Settings → Developers → API → + Create key.
items.why: Gives the API key location, Settings → Developers → API. Matches claim's key part.

items.quote: Sign up for Cloud in under a minute and start your 30-day trial.
items.why: Sign up and start 30-day trial. Self-serve trial stated. No card detail.

items.quote: Host Twenty on your own infrastructure at no cost:
items.why: Self-host free only. Says nothing about credentials or trial gate.

items.quote: Both are available as REST and GraphQL.
items.why: Confirms REST and GraphQL. Breadth, CRUD scope, batch limits not shown.

items.quote: This is how you programmatically change your data model.
items.why: Data model change mention is related to Metadata API. Doesn't name REST or GraphQL.

items.quote: Use your **workspace URL** (the URL you use to access Twenty) as the MCP endpoint.
items.why: Workspace URL as MCP endpoint shows MCP exists. Vendor-official and exact URL not stated.

items.quote: Request scopes as a space-separated string: scope=api profile
items.why: OAuth scope syntax fragment. Nothing about verdict or build_now.
